images.title: Start with the box you can fill
images.purpose: Shows a four row pyramid where the bottom right box can be filled at once, because 9 sits above 7 and that box.
images.composition: One four row pyramid in the centre, with one small equation beside the filled box.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Ten square boxes stacked as a pyramid: bottom row of four boxes, then three, then two, then one on top, each box centred over the join of the two boxes below it. Bottom row left to right: 5, empty, 7, 2. Third row left to right: empty, empty, 9. Second row left to right: 40, empty. Top box: empty. Empty boxes have thin grey (#6B7280) outlines and nothing inside. The boxes holding 9 and 7 have teal (#0072B2) outlines. The bottom right box holding 2 has a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline and the 2 is in reddish purple. To the right of that box, the equation 9 − 7 = 2 in reddish purple. Exactly 10 boxes, 5 of them empty; no arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Start where a box and one of its two parts are known.
